earlier_scan.source_named: Fricke 2019 LOT thesis WAS read (lotpublications.nl): its stress section (3.2.5) describes Central Lembata only, not Ile Ape; only other ref is Keraf 1978 on Lamalera. No description of Ile Ape stress found.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026 [2025]. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (LSP 526).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only the areal remark (sec. 3.2.1, p. 115): 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.' Ile Ape occurs only in the classification tree ('Adonara-Ile Ape Lamaholot > Ile Ape Lamaholot [ila] **ʔ > ∅'), footnote 22 (44% lexical similarity with Kedang, Keraf 1978: 448) and the language table (source Keraf 1978). No Ile Ape-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page ilea1237 Ile Ape (refs: Fricke 2019 pp. 171-228; Grimes & Edwards 2025 pp. 116-122; Eberhard et al. 2025)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; lists no descriptive work beyond the classification references; Glottolog 5.1 export gives Keraf 1978 (wordlist overview) as the sole reference.

sources.citation: Michels, Jos. 2017. A cross-dialectal sketch of Western Lamaholot. Leiden University RMA thesis.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.2.1 Stress, p. 25: 'Stress in Lamaholot is not usually contrastive. The general rule is that stress is on the penultimate syllable, but even neighbouring dialects may vary in the details.. Rather less is known about stress in most dialects outside of Flores.' Generic Lamaholot; Ile Ape and the Lembata dialects (other than Lamalera vowel length) are not discussed.

sources.citation: Krausse, Daniel. 2016. A brief grammar of the Eastern Atadei language of Lembata, Indonesia. Linguistik Indonesia 34(2).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ile Ape named only in the list of Lembata languages ('West Lembata, Ile Ape, Levuka..'); stress remarks concern Eastern Atadei only.

sources.citation: Marolly, Elizabeth Rilyn Marsella, Sebastianus Fernandez, Yosep B. Kroon & Zantty O. Padahana. 2024. A syntactic analysis of the basic sentence patterns in Ile Ape dialect of Lamaholot language. Sintaksis 2(3): 105-121. doi:10.61132/sintaksis.v2i3.890
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Syntax only (five basic sentence patterns); sec. 2.6 gives background (Ile Ape = Nusa Tadon, c. 18,000 speakers, north Lembata near the Ile Ape volcano); examples carry no stress marks; references list no prior Ile Ape phonology.

sources.citation: Nugroho, Zefanya Christiady & Heppy Christinawati Silaen. 2024. Dinamika ketahanan bahasa-bahasa rumpun Lamaholot di Lembata. Linguistik Indonesia 42(1). doi:10.26499/li.v42i1.578
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Participatory vitality survey (Ile Ape surveyed at desa Tokojaeng; vitality revised from Ethnologue 6b to 6a); no phonology.

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L.A. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. LOT Dissertation Series 544. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress section 3.2.5 (p. 49) describes Central Lembata (levu1239) only. Ile Ape appears solely as wordlist lect 'ia' (ISO ila, source Keraf 1978b) in the appendix source table and in comparative word tables (e.g. p. 69); no Ile Ape stress statement.
